title: Justice Department’s Statement on Its Investigation of Vistra’s Acquisition of Cogentrix
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Statement on Its Investigation of Vistra’s Acquisition of Cogentrix Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward, Jr. of the U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Cogentrix Energy (Cogentrix) by Vistra Corp. (Vistra) (together, the “Parties”): “Electricity customers in Maine, New Hampshire, and across New England will benefit from continued competition to generate affordable electricity. As New Englanders turn on the heat for the coming winter season, it’s critical that consumers not bear the risks of higher electricity bills. The Division anticipates that Vistra’s divestitures will save consumers throughout New England tens of millions of dollars annually in electricity bills.” “The Division has developed sophisticated methods for reviewing electricity generation mergers; these tools benefit American consumers and businesses that depend on affordable power,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General G. Charles Beller of the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division. “Given the importance of affordable electricity for consumers, the Division will continue to monitor electricity transactions and the electricity sector as a whole. The Division will not hesitate to take appropriate action to safeguard competition in electricity markets.” On Jan. 5, Vistra announced an agreement to acquire Cogentrix from Quantum Capital Group. Both firms are electricity generation companies that compete in wholesale electricity and electric capacity auctions run by Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs) or Independent System Operators (ISOs). RTOs and ISOs are nonprofit organizations responsible for managing and operating electric power grids within specific regions of the United States. These organizations also rely on internal or external market monitors, who are responsible for overseeing and evaluating the electricity market’s performance. Vistra’s acquisition of Cogentrix combines overlapping electricity generation asset portfolios in three different RTO/ISOs: PJM Interconnection LLC (which covers portions of the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic); ISO New England Inc. (ISO-NE); and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas. As required by federal law, Vistra and Cogentrix filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for approval of the transaction. During FERC’s review process, the Internal Market Monitor of ISO-NE submitted comments to FERC stating that Vistra’s acquisition of Cogentrix raised concerns about a potential reduction in competition that may enable the exercise of market power in ISO-NE. While the Parties’ FERC application was pending, Vistra unilaterally decided to sell its Casco Bay Energy facility (Casco Bay) in ISO-NE. FERC acknowledged that it “consider[ed]” Vistra’s unilateral decision and approved the transaction without conditions. Following FERC’s approval, the Division continued its investigation to assess whether Vistra would have the ability and incentive to withhold electricity from the ISO-NE market after acquiring Cogentrix, notwithstanding the Casco Bay facility divestiture. The Division conducted a thorough investigation, reviewing thousands of documents, performing sophisticated economic modeling, and conducting extensive interviews with industry participants. After evaluating this evidence, the Division remained concerned that the portfolio of electricity generation units that would be combined in ISO-NE may result in a substantial lessening of competition, even with the sale of the Casco Bay facility. The Division’s legal and economic analysis followed the framework for evaluating electricity mergers described in the Division’s 2025 settlement complaint and competitive impact statement regarding Constellation Energy Corp.’s acquisition of Calpine Corp. Vistra and Cogentrix then unilaterally decided to sell Cogentrix’s gas-fired combined-cycle power plant in Rumford, Maine, which would reduce the combined firm’s ability and incentive to withhold electricity and raise prices in ISO-NE. The Division will continue to monitor Vistra’s sale of the Rumford facility. In the interim period, Vistra and Cogentrix must continue to abide by all applicable FERC regulations. The Division emphasizes that the outcome of this investigation is limited to its facts. Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Antitrust Components Antitrust Division Office of the Associate Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1305

title: Israeli National Extradited to Face Charges for Stealing Nearly $3M in Virtual Currency Heist
body: Press Release Israeli National Extradited to Face Charges for Stealing Nearly $3M in Virtual Currency Heist Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Alexander Gurevich, 49, an Israeli national, had his initial appearance today in the Northern District of California on a 2023 indictment that charged him for exploiting the Nomad Bridge’s self-executing computer program, also known as a smart contract, to steal $2.89 million in virtual currency.Gurevich was arrested in May 2025 in Israel and was recently extradited to the United States. According to the indictment, on or about Aug. 1, 2022, Gurevich is alleged to have executed four exploit transactions from the Nomad Bridge and transferred a total of 103 WBTC (Wrapped Bitcoin) and 300 WETH (Wrapped Ether) from Nomad’s virtual currency address to a virtual currency address controlled by Gurevich through unauthorized and non-authenticated transactions. The estimated value of this virtual currency was approximately $2,894,390 at the time of the transactions. Shortly after he stole this virtual currency, Gurevich conducted a number of financial transactions to convert the virtual currency to other types of virtual currency, including Bitcoin, and continued to transfer the funds to multiple virtual currency addresses in order to conceal and disguise the nature, location, source, ownership, and control of the proceeds of his unlawful activity. Gurevich is charged with causing damage to a protected computer, interstate transportation of stolen money, and money laundering. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine for causing damage to a protected computer, as well as for interstate transportation of stolen money, and 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine for money laundering. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Craig H. Missakian for the Northern District of California, and Special Agent in Charge Scott R. Schelble of the FBI made the announcement. The FBI is investigating the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs and Israeli authorities provided substantial assistance. Trial Attorneys Jessica Peck and Ethan Cantor of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and the Northern District of California are prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Cybercrime Components Criminal Division Criminal - Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - California, Northern Press Release Number: 26-1300

title: Federal Jury Convicts Georgia Felon for Illegal Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Federal Jury Convicts Georgia Felon for Illegal Possession of a Firearm Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Jonathan Deon Morehead, 38, of Atlanta, Georgia, was found guilty by a federal jury in Tallahassee following a trial for possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The verdict was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “The aggressive prosecutors in my office are relentlessly pursuing the dangerous criminals threatening the safety of our communities, and we continue to deliver successful prosecutions to send those criminals to federal prison where they belong. This case reaffirms what should already be abundantly clear: the Northern District of Florida has zero-tolerance for crime, and we won’t stop until we deliver the safe, crime-free streets that our citizens deserve.” Trial testimony revealed that on May 28, 2026, during an operation to locate possible victims of human trafficking, law enforcement initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle driven by the defendant. A female occupant was also inside. During a probable cause search of the vehicle, officers found a loaded handgun in the center console. The defendant tried to convince law enforcement that he was allowed to shoot firearms at gun ranges in Georgia, despite being a convicted felon. He also admitted that his fingerprints and DNA would be on the firearm but claimed the firearm belonged to the female passenger. Evidence recovered from the defendant’s phone ultimately confirmed that the defendant arranged the purchase of the firearm months earlier in February 2026. Because the defendant was a convicted felon, he could not legally possess a firearm. Morehead faces up to 15 years’ imprisonment. The case was jointly investigated by the Tallahassee Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. Assistant United States Attorney Emma Schwan is prosecuting the case. Sentencing is scheduled for January 28, 2027, at 3:00 pm in the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Robert L. Hinkle. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access available public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . Contact United States Attorney’s Office Northern District of Florida USAFLN.Press.Office@usdoj.gov X: @USAO_NDFL Updated October 30, 2026 Topics Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Florida, Northern

title: Byrd Gang Members  Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for 2017 Double Homicide Committed Outside Edna Karr High School Basketball Game
body: Press Release Byrd Gang Members  Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for 2017 Double Homicide Committed Outside Edna Karr High School Basketball Game Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS – U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle announced that TERRAN WILLIAMS, a/k/a “Funky” (“WILLIAMS,”) TYRONE BOVIA, a/k/a “Sixx” (“BOVIA, ”) and JAVONTA DOLEMAN, a/k/a “Dutt” (“DOLEMAN,”) all from New Orleans, were sentenced to life imprisonment by United States District Judge Jane Triche Milazzo. In April 2025, WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN were found guilty by a jury after a multi-week trial of various violations, including RICO conspiracy, drug trafficking conspiracy, firearms conspiracy and Violent Crime in Aid of Racketeering (VCAR) murder. “The sentences of life imprisonment for WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN ensures that these violent murderers and drug traffickers will spend the rest of their lives in federal prison,” stated U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. “These prosecutions and sentences are examples of the federal government’s dedication to bring individuals who wreak havoc on our community to justice.” All three defendants were members of the Byrd Gang, also known as M3, MagFischer, 315 and Piff Gang, which operated primarily out of the former Magnolia Housing Development, but additionally had ties to the Westbank.  Its members distributed drugs- heroin, fentanyl, crack cocaine and marijuana- daily, and always possessed firearms. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN participated in numerous drug trafficking activities and violent crimes and acted as gunmen for the Byrd Gang. On January 31, 2017, Lawrence Williams, IV, and Wynston Jackson, a/k/a “Ghost,” were shot and killed by the three defendants shortly after leaving an Edna Karr High School basketball game.  Jackson was a member of the rival Ghost Gang, sometimes referred to as the Goonie Gang, while Williams was an associate of Jackson. When Williams and Jackson left the basketball game and sat in a car in front of the school, WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN approached the car with two rifles and a handgun and unloaded a torrent of bullets.  Jackson attempted to return fire with his nine-millimeter handgun but was shot and killed on the scene. Williams, who was also shot, later died at the hospital. TYRONE BOVIA was also convicted for his role in another shooting that he committed in May 2017 at an apartment complex, where another Ghost Gang member, resided and was the intended target. BOVIA’S companion and fellow Byrd Gang member, Terrence Augustine, was shot and killed during this incident by return fire.  Byrd Gang member, James Alexander, has additionally pled guilty to this shooting. During the trial, evidence was presented that showed a slew of back-and-forth retaliatory shootings between the Byrd Gang and the Ghost Gang, much of which was fueled by social media posts, rap music, and videos.  Numerous individuals from both gangs have been shot and killed, and many innocent bystanders have likewise been shot during these inner-city rivalries. During the investigation, dozens of firearms, most with large-capacity magazines, as well as hundreds of rounds of ammunition, have been recovered from Byrd Gang members, including from the three defendants. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN faced a mandatory life sentence for the Edna Karr murders which were charged in Counts 4 and 6 of the Superseding Indictment and were sentenced accordingly. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN were additionally sentenced to life imprisonment for Count 1 (RICO conspiracy), and to 240 months for Counts 2 (drug conspiracy) and 3 (firearm conspiracy). BOVIA was also sentenced to 120 months imprisonment for discharging a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and crime of violence, which was charged in Count 9. This sentence was imposed consecutively to all other sentences. U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle praised the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, especially the New Orleans Gang Task Force, the New Orleans Police Department, Sulphur Police Department, Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office, Louisiana State Police, and the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office in investigating this matter.  Assistant United States Attorneys Elizabeth Privitera, David Haller and Sarah Dawkins are in charge of the prosecution. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . *      *      * Contact Shane M. title: Kansas man pleads guilty to illegal gun possession
body: Press Release Kansas man pleads guilty to illegal gun possession Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas TOPEKA, KAN. – A Kansas man pleaded guilty to illegally possessing a firearm while facing criminal charges. According to court documents, Leonard Rrapaj, 62, of Topeka pleaded guilty to one count of illegal receipt of a firearm while under indictment. In August 2025, a search warrant was executed at Rrapaj’s business and residence, located at the Topeka Sports Cabaret. In Rrapaj’s bedroom, law enforcement found a firearm. At the time, the defendant was under indictment for federal charges. Rrapaj is scheduled to be sentenced on February 10, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Lindsey Debenham is prosecuting the case. ### Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Kansas

title: DOJ’s Fraud Division and the United States Attorney’s Office for the District Minnesota Uncover Nearly $30 Million in Benefits Fraud in Enforcement Surge
body: Press Release DOJ’s Fraud Division and the United States Attorney’s Office for the District Minnesota Uncover Nearly $30 Million in Benefits Fraud in Enforcement Surge Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota The U.S. Attorney’s Office and Fraud Division have issued over 1,000 subpoenas for the purpose of uncovering fraud in Minnesota just this year alone MINNEAPOLIS – The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota announced a series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving taxpayer-funded Medicaid and SNAP programs. Between Sept. 30, and today, the Fraud Division and the District of Minnesota have charged, convicted, or sentenced 13 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $83 million in intended losses to the federal government, including approximately $29.1 million in fraud uncovered in the newly charged cases. This effort is a result of a partnership between prosecutors from DOJ’s Fraud Division and the U.S. Attorney’s Office. This year alone, the DOJ has issued over 1,000 subpoenas and executed over 40 premises warrants for the purpose of uncovering fraud in Minnesota. “Minnesota is the epicenter for fraud in America,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. “The Trump administration’s crackdown is working, and the results speak for themselves. Through the Minnesota Fraud Task Force we are systematically dismantling schemes preying on Americans. Backed by more than a thousand subpoenas and 40 warrants, the message is simple: No one stealing from taxpayer-funded programs is safe.” “The alarming concentration of fraud targeting taxpayer-funded programs in Minnesota demands a coordinated and sustained response,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “We are working with our law enforcement partners to uncover alleged fraud, protect public funds, and hold offenders accountable. We will continue these efforts until these schemes are dismantled and taxpayer dollars are protected from abuse in Minnesota.” “The cases highlighted today represent my office’s unwavering commitment to protect the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs,” said U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota. “These defendants stole money meant for the vulnerable, and they will be brought to justice.” “The FBI is laser-focused on combatting frauds against the American taxpayer,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson. “Through our partnerships with other federal, state, and local partners, we continue to see great progress in eliminating the fraud that has taken so much from our children and those in need of the critical services and resources that taxpayers fund. As we continue to conduct investigations and make arrests, fraudsters should know: justice will find you.” “Fraud against taxpayer-funded programs leaves a financial trail, and IRS-CI is built to follow it,” said Chief Jarod Koopman of IRS Criminal Investigation. “Our agents trace funds through bank accounts, businesses, shell companies, digital records, and assets to determine who benefited, where the money went, and how it was concealed. People can add layers of transactions and entities, but they cannot erase the underlying economic reality. Working with our federal, state, and local partners, we will continue turning complex financial activity into evidence and helping protect funds intended for children, patients, and families.” “Fraud is not a victimless crime. It steals from citizens, diverts resources from families who need them, and undermines public trust in the programs and institutions that serve our communities,” said HSI St. Paul Special Agent in Charge Travis Pickard. “HSI St. Paul is proud to stand with our law enforcement partners to disrupt fraud networks, protect honest businesses, and hold offenders accountable. We will continue to follow the money, follow the evidence, and protect our communities.” Photos of law enforcement seizing potential evidence during fraud enforcement operation on October 29, 2026 Charges Shaakir Mohamud Ibrahim , 54, of Pelican Rapids, Minnesota, was arrested on Sept. 30, after spending nearly 10 months as a fugitive in Kenya. On Sept. 29, Ibrahim was charged by indictment with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering and money laundering in connection with his role in a $1.1 million scheme to defraud the Federal Child Nutrition Program through Feeding Our Future. For four months, Ibrahim and his co-conspirators claimed to be serving more than 3,000 meals to children every day, in the small town of Pelican Rapids, Minnesota through Bilaal Mosque in Pelican Rapids, and another 3,000 meals per day at the Multicultural Resource Center in Moorhead, Minnesota.  As part of the scheme, Bilaal and MRC submitted fake meal counts and rosters to Feeding Our Future. After receiving more than $1.1 million in reimbursements through Feeding Our Future, Ibrahim laundered his share of the proceeds through large check payments to himself and his son, as well as the purchase of a property in Kenya and a car. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys for the District of Minnesota Rebecca E. Kline, Matthew C. Murphy, and Austin L. Bowyer and investigated by FBI, IRS-CI, and USPIS. Emily Marice Ravits , 74, of Tucson, Arizona, was charged by indictment on Oct. 22, with conspiracy to defraud the United States and to make false statements related to health care matters and six counts of false statements relating to health care matters in connection with a $7.7 million scheme to interfere with the lawful government functions of HHS and CMS in their administration and oversight of Medicaid. As alleged in the indictment, Emily Marice Ravits was a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and Qualified Supervising Professional (QSP) in Minnesota. In that role, she agreed to serve as the QSP for multiple providers of autism therapy without actually performing the duties required of QSPs and permitting providers to submit claims for services that were not performed or that were not properly reimbursable and submit false certifications on individual treatment plans to justify the continuation of autism therapy services. As a result, false and fraudulent claims were submitted Medicaid for EIDBI autism therapy by providers for services that were not actually eligible for reimbursement. This case is being jointly prosecuted by the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota and investigated by FBI, HHS-OIG, and IRS-CI. Feisal Mohamed Elmi , 46, of New Brighton, Minnesota, was charged by indictment on Oct. 22, with eleven counts of health care fraud, in connection with an $8.2 million scheme to defraud the Minnesota Medicaid EIDBI autism therapy program. As alleged in the indictment, Feisal Mohamed Elmi submitted fraudulent claims to the Minnesota EIDBI program by billing for services that were not rendered and for services purportedly provided by employees while they were traveling and located outside of the United States. In addition, almost every claim was billed at the same amount regardless of the service provided or the number of hours of service provided. This case is being jointly prosecuted by the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota and investigated by FBI, HHS-OIG, and IRS-CI. Habiba Mohamed , 58, of Coon Rapids, Minnesota was charged by information on Oct. 29, with conspiracy to defraud the United States in connection with a $19.1 million scheme to defraud the Minnesota Medicaid EIDBI autism therapy program. As alleged in the information, Habiba Mohamed and her co-conspirators (previously charged by indictment) submitted fraudulent claims related to the EIDBI program and she, personally, paid kickbacks to the parents of Medicaid recipients in exchange for being able to submit claims for services. This case is being jointly prosecuted by the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota and investigated by FBI, HHS-OIG, and IRS-CI. Faiza Osman Ahmed , 41, of Richfield, Minnesota, was charged by indictment on Oct. 28, with six counts of health care fraud in connection with an approximately $10 million scheme to defraud multiple Minnesota Medicaid programs. As alleged in the indictment, Faiza Osman Ahmed submitted fraudulent claims related to the Minnesota Individualized Home Supports, Personal Care Assistance, and Night Supervision programs. She did so by, among other things, billing for services that were not rendered and for services purportedly provided recipients in their homes while they were traveling, while providers were actually working other jobs, and for recipients who never got the billed-for services. This case is being jointly prosecuted by the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota and investigated by FBI, HHS-OIG, VA-OIG, HSI, and the State of Minnesota Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Jama Yusuf Mohamod , 68, of Maple Grove, Minnesota, was charged by indictment on Oct. 28, with eight counts of health care fraud in connection with a scheme to submit approximately $3.2 million in fraudulent claims to the Minnesota Medicaid Integrated Community Supports Program. As alleged in the indictment, Jama Yusuf Mohamod submitted fraudulent claims related to the Minnesota ICS program. He did so by, among other things, billing for services that were not rendered and for services purportedly provided to recipients in their homes while they were traveling. He also used Super Intelligence to create fake patient notes to justify his claims. This case is being jointly prosecuted by the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota. Ahmed Abdul Razaq Al Obaidi , 49, of Blaine, Minnesota, and Muhammad Abdullah Kahn , were charged on Oct. 21, by complaint with knowingly and unlawfully transferring SNAP benefits. The charges resulted from joint USDA‑OIG and Homeland Security Operation Cold SNAP, which identified local businesses engaged in fraudulent use and trafficking of SNAP benefits, during which AK Tobacco LLC was identified as a location involved in cash trafficking of EBT benefits. Minnesota business records identified Al Obaidi as the manager of AK Tobacco, LLC, and investigators also identified Muhammad Abdullah Kahn as a clerk associated with the store. Al Obaidi was identified as engaging in EBT/SNAP benefit fraud and was arrested on Oct. 21. This case is being prosecuted by First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Minnesota Joseph S. Teirab and investigated by USDA-OIG and HSI. Convictions Muna Wais Fidhin, 45, of Savage, Minnesota, was found guilty of three counts of wire fraud, four counts of federal programs bribery, and two counts of money laundering on Oct. 21, after a three-week jury trial. As evidenced at trial, between October 2020 and February 2022, Fidhin participated in a scheme to defraud the Federal Child Nutrition Program through the sponsorship of both Feeding Our Future and Partners in Nutrition. Fidhin submitted fake meal counts and food invoices to Feeding Our Future, claiming to have served 500 meals, 7 days per week, out of her food site M5 Café – a small hallway café at the M Health Fairview Burnsville Clinic.  She also paid $26,000 in bribes to Feeding Our Future employee Abdikerm Eidleh to facilitate her participation in the scheme. Later, Fidhin created a second fraudulent food site, M5 Care, which participated in the food program through Partners in Nutrition. Fidhin claimed to have served over 337,000 meals in nine months, entitling her to nearly $1 million dollars in reimbursement. As evidenced at trial, Fidhin spent the fraud proceeds to pay off the mortgage on her house in Savage, to send money overseas, and to pay off her Lexus SUV. Fidhin will be sentenced at a later date. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys for the District of Minnesota Rebecca E. Kline, Matthew C. Murphy, and Austin L. Bowyer and investigated by FBI, IRS-CI, and USPIS. Nicole Lee Slegers , 48, and Shaun Hubert Slegers , 37, both of Arco, Minnesota, pleaded guilty to one count each of conspiracy to commit wire fraud before U.S. District Judge Donovan W. Frank on Oct. 28. According to court documents, from approximately June 2021 through March 2023, they conspired to devise and carry out a scheme to defraud the estates of recently deceased recipients of Minnesota’s Medicaid program. Nicole Slegers, who worked in various roles at Southwest HHS from 2018 through 2023, used her position to fraudulently obtain vehicles by falsely telling authorized representatives that the vehicles would be sold and credited to the recipients’ accounts. Nicole and Shaun Slegers intimidated and harassed grieving family members to induce quick transfers, gaining approximately $144,524 through fraudulent transfers of at least 14 vehicles and forging signatures to transfer titles. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Minnesota Rebecca E. Kline and investigated by the FBI. Sentences Salim Ahmed Said , 37, of Plymouth Minnesota, was sentenced to 360 months in prison on Oct. 28, by United States District Judge Nancy E. Brasel, in connection with his role in the $250 million scheme to defraud the Federal Child Nutrition Program through Feeding Our Future. After a six-week jury trial in early 2025, Said (along with his co-defendant, Aimee Bock) was convicted on one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, four counts of wire fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit federal programs bribery, eight counts of bribery, one count conspiracy to commit money laundering and five counts of money laundering.  As proven at trial, Said’s Safari Restaurant enrolled in the Federal Child Nutrition Program under the sponsorship of Feeding Our Future in April 2020. By July 2020, Said fraudulently claimed to be serving meals to 5,000 children per day, seven days a week. In total, Said claimed to have served over 3.9 million meals to children from the Safari Restaurant food site between April 2020 and November 2021. Said also claimed that Safari Restaurant provided more than 2.2 million meals to other food sites involved in Feeding Our Future’s fraud scheme. Said and his co-conspirators created numerous shell companies to enroll in the program as food program sites, and to receive and launder the proceeds of their fraudulent scheme.  In total, Said facilitated over $44 million in fraud proceeds through the Federal Child Nutrition Program.  This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys for the District of Minnesota Rebecca E. Kline, Matthew C. Murphy, and Austin L. Bowyer and investigated by FBI, IRS-CI, and USPIS. Salim Said’s properties, purchased with ill-gotten funds Luxury items purchased with stolen funds by Salim Said Said Farah , 44, of Minneapolis, Minnesota, was sentenced to 78 months and a $40,000 fine in prison on Oct. 30, for bribery of a juror. Beginning in April 2024, Farah and several co-defendants were on trial in the United States District Court for the District of Minnesota for various fraud and money laundering charges stemming from a widespread scheme to defraud the Federal Child Nutrition Program. The day after closing arguments in the fraud trial, Farah and his co-conspirators attempted to bribe one of the jurors. Farah helped gather $200,000 in cash, which a co-conspirator delivered to the juror’s home along with a message that the juror would receive more money if she voted to acquit Farah and his co-defendants. The juror immediately reported the attempted bribe to law enforcement. The following morning, the bribe attempt was discussed in open court and the Court ordered Farah and his co-defendants to surrender their phones to law enforcement. Before surrendering his phone, however, Farah deleted incriminating text messages. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys for the District of Minnesota Rebecca E. Kline, Matthew C. Murphy, and Austin L. Bowyer and investigated by FBI, IRS-CI, and USPIS. Forfeiture Three real properties , located in Minneapolis, Minnesota, valued at approximately $519,000, were encumbered through the lis pendens and named as defendants in a civil forfeiture action filed on Oct. 19, identifying each as having been purchased with proceeds from the Feeding Our Future fraud scheme. Law Enforcement Partners Participation: FBI, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG), IRS-CI, HSI, USPIS, Veterans Affairs Office of Inspector General (VA-OIG), Minnesota Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. In May, the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force charged 15 defendants as part of the largest Medicaid fraud takedown in state history. The Strike Force also joined four cases previously charged by the U.S. Attorney’s Office. Since then, 16 defendants have been convicted. In addition, over the past 110 days alone, courts have imposed approximately 550 months of imprisonment on defendants involved in Minnesota fraud schemes, including those charged by the U.S. Attorney’s Office in the unprecedented Feeding Our Future investigations. Since August, the Fraud Division, including the Health Care Strike Force and Minnesota Fraud Task Force, has also actively investigated a wide range of fraud matters, using every available tool to identify wrongdoing, hold offenders accountable, and advance dozens of ongoing investigations. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment, information, or complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Forty-two Alleged Gang Members and Associates Charged with Trafficking Fentanyl and Methamphetamine Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Forty-two Alleged Gang Members and Associates Charged with Trafficking Fentanyl and Methamphetamine Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Four federal grand jury indictments charge 42 alleged members and associates of various San Diego County street gangs, including an increasingly violent and sophisticated Poway gang called Varrio Hidden Hills, with distributing large amounts of methamphetamine and fentanyl. In a coordinated takedown on Wednesday and Thursday, hundreds of FBI agents, members of the North County Regional Gang Task Force and federal, state, and local law enforcement officials arrested 35 defendants and executed 10 search warrants on homes and vehicles in Poway, Lemon Grove, San Diego, National City, Chula Vista, Imperial Beach, El Cajon, Oceanside, Escondido, Vista, Temecula, Murrieta, Riverside, and Tulare. As of 2:30 p.m. today, seven defendants were still being sought. Authorities seized drugs, guns, ammunition and cash during the takedown and throughout the two-year investigation. FBI agents came under fire while serving an arrest warrant at 6:10 a.m. Wednesday at a home in Lemon Grove. After agents identified themselves pursuant to standard protocol, multiple shots were fired in their direction from inside the residence through the front door and front window. No one was hit, and FBI agents retreated to safety after briefly returning fire. Tactical law enforcement personnel responded, and the target of the arrest warrant was taken into custody after coming out of the residence. The shooting is under investigation. “These arrests strike at the heart of this violent, sophisticated, Mexican Mafia connected criminal gang,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon, “The dangers our agents faced is a troubling reminder of the threats gang members pose, but also, the courage of those who confront them. We are grateful every agent is going home to their loved ones.” “Cases like this are only possible because of the outstanding partnerships across our federal, state, and local law enforcement community,” said Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI San Diego Field Office. “Working together, we dismantled a violent criminal operation led by an assessed gang leader with suspected cartel associations, responsible for moving dangerous narcotics into our neighborhoods. This investigation also showed the level of violence these groups are willing to use when our agents came under fire while working to protect this community. Through unwavering teamwork, we stopped a network driving deadly drugs and violence into our neighborhoods. We will continue to use every lawful tool available to stop those threatening the safety of the people we serve.” “San Diego continues to be safer because of the law enforcement partnerships we have in this region.  The deputies, analysts and Sheriff leadership assigned to the North County Gang Task Force contributed their dedication and talents to this very complex case involving dozens of defendants in an investigation that crossed borders and multiple jurisdictions,” said San Diego County Sheriff Kelly Martinez. “I commend all the agencies and investigative teams involved in this effort and I’m grateful to see these dangerous individuals facing criminal consequences for their actions.” “This operation highlights the strength of collaboration among local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies in combating violent crime, dismantling criminal organizations, and removing dangerous drugs from our communities,” said CHP Chief Brandon Shipwash. “As California’s state police, the CHP remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners, utilizing our statewide resources and investigative expertise to hold those responsible accountable and protect the communities we serve.” “We extend our sincere appreciation to our federal partners for their outstanding cooperation, coordination, and commitment throughout this operation and successful takedown,” said Oceanside Chief of Police Taurino Valdovinos. “This operation sends a clear message: criminal activity will not be tolerated in San Diego County, and we remain committed to working together to hold those who threaten our communities accountable.” The arrests arise out of an FBI investigation that was initiated in mid-2024 into the Varrio Hidden Hills criminal street gang and associated illegal activity in Poway - specifically a senior-ranking documented member of the gang, John Marquez, and his associates. The investigation quickly expanded to all of San Diego County and other parts of California due to the expansive and overlapping criminal networks. During the two-year investigation, FBI agents and task force members learned that Marquez was the alleged leader of an international drug-trafficking organization and was associated with the Mexican Mafia. Marquez allegedly organized a multi-tiered distribution scheme using other San Diego County gang members and associates as distributors. Marquez oversaw separate chains of supply, set pricing, and collected drug proceeds to take back to his sources of supply in Mexico, according to court documents. He travelled continuously to and from Mexico to meet with his cartel-linked sources of supply and facilitate the importation of narcotics into the United States. The Mexican Mafia, a.k.a. “La Eme,” is a U.S.-based prison gang that has immense control over Hispanic street gangs in Southern California, directing illegal activities from prisons and collecting a portion of the proceeds from drug trafficking, illegal gambling, and other crimes committed on the streets. In addition to control over U.S.-based street gangs, the Mexican Mafia has ties to foreign terrorist organization (FTO)-designated criminal networks, including the Sinaloa Cartel, Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), and Mara Salvatrucha 13 (MS-13). The investigation uncovered an extensive operation funneling various narcotics from drug trafficking networks based in Mexico across the border and into San Diego and surrounding communities for further distribution. According to court documents, many of the defendants have criminal records that include robberies, assaults, and other violent and dangerous conduct. The evidence also reflected that Marquez continually collected drug proceeds from his sub-distributors to send back to his sources of supply in Mexico. For example, in one series of communications with one of his primary sources of methamphetamine and fentanyl, Marquez advised that he was preparing to go down to Mexico to pick up fentanyl and stated, “I have to count some money and send it to Sinaloa.” Court documents said Marquez’s organization earned substantial profits; the evidence reflected that Marquez regularly supplied methamphetamine at a price of between $750-$900 per pound, in addition to his profits from dealing fentanyl – which he worked with others to import for a price of $12,500 to $13,000 per kilogram. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jill Streja and Shivanjali A. Sewak. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Diego comprises agents and officers from FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, DEA, ATF, U.S. Marshals, Department of Defense, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Interpol, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) program, created by Congress with the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1988, provides assistance to Federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies operating in areas determined to be critical drug-trafficking regions of the United States. This grant program is administered by the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). There are currently 33 HIDTAs, and HIDTA-designated counties are located in 50 states, as well as in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and the District of Columbia. title: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz issues statement regarding Harris County DA indicting ICE agent
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz issues statement regarding Harris County DA indicting ICE agent Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Texas HOUSTON – “Disappointed in his inability to swiftly bring charges in the tragic Salgado shooting in July, the Harris County District Attorney now appears determined to put a different federal agent’s scalp on the wall. This time, he’s pursuing what looks like a political prosecution of an ICE agent for doing his job—exactly what his allies have been agitating for. “My office was not consulted or even notified before this indictment. The DA’s office never contacted us. That tells you something about the approach they’ve taken. “I have personally conducted a preliminary review of the facts and law. Given what I know, I see no basis for federal charges at this time. We will, of course, continue to evaluate any relevant evidence and legal issues within our jurisdiction. “Federal agents should not be turned into political trophies for doing the difficult and dangerous work of enforcing federal law. We stand with ICE and all our federal law enforcement partners.” Updated October 30, 2026 Component USAO - Texas, Southern

title: Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison
body: Press Release Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that DANNY TURKVAN, also known as “Smooth” 55, of Stamford, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to an additional 14 months of imprisonment for distributing crack cocaine after he had been sentenced in another federal case and prior to reporting to prison. On August 13, 2025, Turkvan was sentenced in Hartford federal court to 46 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for his participation in a southwestern Connecticut narcotics trafficking conspiracy.  Turkvan, who was released on a $150,000 bond, was ordered to report to prison on October 16, 2025.  An investigation revealed that Turkvan continued to distribute narcotics after his August 2025 sentencing.  Stamford Police arrested Turkvan on state charges on October 11, 2025, and seized crack cocaine that he intended to distribute. Turkvan has been detained since his arrest.  On July 8, 2026, he pleaded guilty in federal court to possession with intent to distribute cocaine base (“crack”). This investigation was conducted by the Stamford Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patricia Stolfi Collins. title: Federal Law Enforcement Initiative Targets Sex Offender Registration Violations and Child Exploitation
body: Press Release Federal Law Enforcement Initiative Targets Sex Offender Registration Violations and Child Exploitation Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri Enforcement effort announced one day before Halloween results in 19 defendants federally charged in October KANSAS CITY, Mo. – The U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri announced today that, as part of its ongoing Project Safe Childhood initiative, federal, state, and local law enforcement partners have conducted a focused enforcement effort targeting individuals who fail to comply with federal sex offender registration requirements and those involved in child exploitation. The initiative was done in conjunction with the U.S. Marshals Service’s Operation Lights Out , which targets sex offenders who are prohibited from participating in Halloween activities, including turning on their porch light to signal that trick-or-treaters are welcome. During October, 19 defendants were charged with either failing to register as required under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act (SORNA), or with various federal child exploitation offenses. Announced one day before Halloween, the enforcement effort underscores the Department of Justice’s commitment to holding offenders accountable, protecting children, and enhancing community safety. “There is no safe harbor for individuals who prey on children or disregard the laws designed to protect our communities,” said R. Matthew Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri. “We will aggressively pursue those who exploit children and hold accountable those who fail to meet their legal obligations as registered sex offenders. Protecting children is not seasonal. It is part of our mission every day of the year.” Below are cases that have been charged because of this initiative: United States v. title: Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy
body: Press Release Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A Florida pharmacist and pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 90 months in prison for her role in illegally dispensing over 300,000 oxycodone 30mg pills to pharmacy patrons who had no medical need for the drug. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Olushola Yusuf, 60, of Tampa, dispensed oxycodone to nearly all of her pharmacy customers. Yusuf charged customers approximately 10 times the typical cost of the drug and required payment from them in cash. In total, Yusuf dispensed at least 335,351 pills of oxycodone 30mg during the conspiracy. Oxycodone 30mg is the maximum strength available of the drug and is both sought after and potentially dangerous due to its potency. It is typically prescribed to seriously ill patients, such as those suffering from chronic cancer pain or traumatic injuries. Photograph of Cash Paid to Yusuf for Illegally Distributing Oxycodone from her Pharmacy Yusuf owned and operated two pharmacies, Boots LLC doing business as, Striderite (Boots) in Margate, and Chans Pharmacy Plus, Inc. (Chans) in Pembroke Pines. Yusuf distributed oxycodone 30mg pills through these pharmacies. Customers drove long distances to have Yusuf fill prescriptions that they could not get filled at any other pharmacy. Some customers paid as much as $1,300 a month in cash to Yusuf for the drugs. And some customers were drug dealers who picked up oxycodone pills purportedly on behalf of dozens of patients at a time who were not present. According to witnesses at trial, Yusuf kept the doors to her pharmacies locked during business hours, directing employees only to open the door for certain identified customers. Yusuf continued to dispense oxycodone in this way even after repeated warnings from her employees and the DEA about the dangers of her pharmacy operations. After a two-week trial in July 2026, the jury convicted Yusuf of conspiracy to illegally distribute drugs and five counts of illegal drug distribution. Yusuf’s co-defendant, Saman Gimenez, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to illegally distribute drugs and is scheduled be sentenced later this year. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida; Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Chief of Operations Matthew W. Allen; FBI Co-Deputy Director Christopher Raia; and Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett for the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) made the announcement. DEA, FBI, and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Trial Attorney Angela Benoit of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Jacqueline DerOvanesian for the Southern District of Florida prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/fraud/health-care-fraud-section . Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1306

title: Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud
body: Press Release Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs An Indian national pleaded guilty today to a $227 million Medicare fraud scheme in which hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries’ personally identifiable information was purchased from a company based in Pakistan and used to bill Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that were never provided. According to court documents and statements made in court, Syed Murtuza Kablazada, 36, an Indian national residing in Des Plaines, Illinois, engaged in a scheme to defraud the Medicare program by submitting false and fraudulent claims for over-the-counter COVID-19 test kits that were not requested by beneficiaries or provided to them. Over the course of six months, starting in January 2023, Kablazada and his co-schemers acquired three Chicago-area laboratories, Chicago Care, V Care, and Al-Ameer. Kablazada then paid approximately $11 million to a purported telemarketing company based in Pakistan to obtain personally identifiable information for hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries. Using those Medicare beneficiaries’ information, Kablazada caused the laboratories to submit $227 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare for test kits that he knew were never requested by or shipped to the Medicare beneficiaries, for which Medicare paid approximately $136 million. To conceal their involvement in this scheme, Kablazada and his co-schemers paid themselves through overseas money transfers and unlicensed money transmitters, and they used the proceeds in part to purchase luxury vehicles. As part of his plea agreement in this case, Kablazada agreed to forfeit over $46 million in fraud proceeds that law enforcement seized from ten bank accounts. Kablazada pleaded guilty to two counts of health care fraud. He is scheduled to be sentenced on a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen of the FBI Chicago Field Office; and Special Agent in Charge Thomas Ethridge of the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) made the announcement. The FBI Chicago Field Office and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Deputy Chief Patrick Mott and Trial Attorney Claire Sobczak Pacelli of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Andres Almendarez for the Northern District of Illinois assisted in investigating and prosecuting this case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1302

title: South Florida Selected as First Pilot Location for National Initiative to Combat Federal Nutrition Assistance Fraud
body: Press Release South Florida Selected as First Pilot Location for National Initiative to Combat Federal Nutrition Assistance Fraud Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida today joined U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Inspector General John Walk and federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to launch the Hunger Assistance Enforcement and Accountability Teams (HEAT) initiative, a coordinated effort to investigate and prosecute fraud involving federal nutrition assistance programs. South Florida will serve as the first pilot location for the national initiative, underscoring the U.S. Attorney’s Office’s commitment to protecting taxpayer-funded assistance programs and holding accountable those who exploit resources intended for vulnerable Americans. The HEAT initiative brings together investigative, prosecutorial, and analytical resources across federal, state, and local agencies to identify, disrupt, and dismantle fraud schemes targeting USDA nutrition assistance programs, including the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP). Through intelligence-driven investigations and coordinated enforcement efforts, HEAT will target individuals and criminal organizations that divert federal assistance funds from those who need them most. South Florida was selected as the initiative’s first pilot location because of its large and diverse population, extensive retail environment, and international connections, which present opportunities for sophisticated fraud schemes. The U.S. Attorney’s Office will work alongside its law enforcement partners to safeguard federal nutrition assistance programs, recover fraudulently obtained funds, and ensure that taxpayer dollars reach the individuals and families these programs are intended to serve. “Federal nutrition assistance programs are a lifeline for families in need, not a payday for fraudsters and criminal organizations,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “When criminals steal from these programs, they rob vulnerable Americans of critical resources and betray the taxpayers who fund them. South Florida is proud to lead the nation as the first HEAT pilot location. Working shoulder to shoulder with USDA Inspector General Walk and our federal, state, and local partners, we will aggressively investigate these schemes, follow the money, dismantle criminal networks, and prosecute those responsible. Our message is simple: If you exploit programs designed to feed Americans in need, expect to face federal justice.” “Criminal organizations and other sophisticated fraudsters are increasingly targeting USDA nutrition assistance programs, like SNAP and CACFP, through sophisticated fraud schemes such as electronic benefit transfer (EBT) theft, SNAP trafficking, retail fraud, identity theft, and cyber methodologies,” Walk said. “We are proud to make this announcement with U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones as we seek to work together on the investigations and ultimate prosecutions of these crimes against the neediest Americans.” The launch included a roundtable with law enforcement leaders to discuss ongoing collaborative strategies. Participating agencies in the inaugural South Florida HEAT meeting included USDA Office of Inspector General, U.S. Attorney's Office Southern District of Florida, Federal Bureau of Investigation Miami, Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, United States Secret Service, Department of Education Office of Inspector General, General Services Administration Office of Inspector General, Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General, Social Security Office of Inspector General, Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecution, Florida Department of Financial Services Criminal Investigations Division, Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office (MDSO), Florida Department of Financial Services, Florida Department of Children and Families, and Defense Criminal Investigative Services. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Benefit Fraud Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026
body:
Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026 Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026 30 October 2026 Headline and core inflation expectations revised upwards for 2026 and 2027, owing primarily to higher energy prices and their indirect effects, with longer-term inflation expectations remaining anchored at 2.0% Near-term GDP growth expectations revised up, primarily reflecting recent data, with increasing growth continued to be expected in the short run Unemployment rate expectations revised up slightly for 2026, but broadly unchanged thereafter Respondents’ expectations for headline inflation, as measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), stood at 3.0% for 2026, 2.6% for 2027 and 2.0% for 2028. Compared with the previous round, these were revised up by 0.3 and 0.4 percentage points for 2026 and 2027 respectively but remained unchanged for 2028. Longer-term expectations (for 2031) remained at 2.0% for both headline and core inflation. A special question, which was also asked in the previous round, concerned the impact of the war in the Middle East. The responses suggested that additional effects of the energy price shock are mainly expected for 2027 but that second-round effects will remain limited. For inflation, the risk balance was tilted to the upside for 2026-28 but remained more balanced thereafter. Respondents expected real GDP growth of 1.0% in 2026 and 1.3% in both 2027 and 2028. Expectations were revised up by 0.4 percentage points for 2026 and by 0.1 percentage points for 2027 compared with the previous survey and were unchanged for 2028. Longer-term growth expectations (for 2031) were revised up by 0.1 percentage points to 1.3%. For real GDP growth, the balance of risks was tilted somewhat to the downside for all horizons. Unemployment rate expectations were slightly higher for 2026 at 6.4%, before declining gradually to 6.1% in the longer term. Table: Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026 (annual percentage changes, unless otherwise indicated) Survey horizon 2026 2027 2028 Longer term 1) HICP inflation SPF Q4 2026 3.0 2.6 2.0 2.0 Changes from the previous survey (Q3 2026) 0.3 0.4 0.0 0.0 Core (HICP excluding energy and food) inflation SPF Q4 2026 2.4 2.5 2.2 2.0 Changes from the previous survey (Q3 2026) 0.0 0.2 0.1 0.0 Real GDP growth SPF Q4 2026 1.0 1.3 1.3 1.3 Changes from the previous survey (Q3 2026) 0.4 0.1 0.0 0.1 Unemployment rate 2) SPF Q4 2026 6.4 6.3 6.2 6.1 Changes from the previous survey (Q3 2026) 0.1 0.0 0.0 0.0 Wage growth SPF Q4 2026 3.3 3.1 2.8 2.7 Changes from the previous survey (Q3 2026) 0.1 0.1 0.0 -0.2 1) Longer-term expectations refer to 2031. 2) As a percentage of the labour force. For media queries, please contact William Lelieveldt , tel.: +49 69 1344 7316. Notes The Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF) for the fourth quarter of 2026 was conducted between 2 and 7 October 2026 and 52 responses were received. The SPF is conducted on a quarterly basis and gathers expectations for inflation, real GDP growth and unemployment in the euro area for several horizons, together with a quantitative assessment of the uncertainty surrounding them. Participants are also asked for other information underlying their forecasts, namely the ECB’s deposit facility rate (DFR), the euro US dollar exchange rate, Brent crude oil prices in USD, wages and the output gap. The survey participants are experts affiliated with financial and non-financial institutions based in Europe. The survey results do not represent the views of the ECB’s decision-making bodies or its staff. The next Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections for the euro area will be published on 18 December 2026. Since 2015, the results of the SPF have been published on the ECB’s website. For surveys prior to the first quarter of 2015, see the ECB’s Monthly Bulletin (2002-14: Q1 – February, Q2 – May, Q3 – August, Q4 – November). The survey report and more detailed data are available via the SPF webpage and the ECB Data Portal .
